story.head: The Sabres need a win
paras: The Flyers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Buffalo on Oct 21. The Flyers (6-11-6) lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Sunday, and the Sabres are winless in four (0-3-1). Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Flyers sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 26th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 69-55, but only 41-38 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 22-11.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). They also get their defensemen shooting (5th), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Flyers’ not so much. As for the Flyers, they play slow, tight games (2nd lowest) and take away shots from the point (4th lowest). They also block more shots than almost anyone (3rd), and the Sabres’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Philadelphia has scored 2.30 goals a game, the second fewest in the league.

Tage Thompson (12 G / 9 A / 21 P in 20 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring. Jack Quinn (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind, with a point in six straight games against Philadelphia. For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov (11 G / 6 A / 17 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring. Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 23 GP) is next in line, with a point in five straight games against Buffalo.
Alex Lyon (0-1-1 / .909 SV% in 2 GS) is expected to start for Buffalo, and Joseph Woll (3-6-2 / .902 SV% in 11 GS) for Philadelphia.
At home, Rick Tocchet likes to send Foerster, Zegras and Konecny out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Krebs and Thompson.
